problem: Relational (spatially constrained) semantic navigation is mostly single-agent, while multi-robot semantic navigation only handles category-level targets or sequential subtasks. Nothing couples multi-robot exploration with instance-specific relation verification over distributed partial evidence.
motivation: Targets are often specified by relations to surrounding objects (e.g. 'a bed between a mirror and a stool'). The target and its supporting objects may lie in different regions and may not be jointly visible from one view, so a robot team could search in parallel and pool complementary observations. This needs task-aware allocation and evidence association across robots and viewpoints.
key_idea: Couple a task-conditioned spatial-semantic field and joint team frontier allocation with candidate-centric relation verification that aggregates instance-consistent evidence across topology nodes.
insight: Ablations show the two parts are complementary. Removing joint allocation lowers SR on both 1-support (0.579 to 0.526) and multi-support (0.447 to 0.395) relations. Removing cross-node aggregation hurts mainly multi-support relations (0.447 to 0.342). The gain over baselines is larger in cross-region episodes (SR 0.746 vs 0.701 for Co-NavGPT), where coordination matters most. Structured, instance-numbered evidence also halves token use versus VLN-Game (Dual). Adding robots beyond two gave no further SPL gain.
method: Task-conditioned spatial-semantic field: text and image encoders (Qwen3-VL-embedding) score cosine similarity between the instruction and topology-node panoramas and object descriptions, spread with a Gaussian kernel over free space into an object heat map that guides evidence acquisition.

Per-robot frontier shortlisting: each frontier gets a score from rollout-predicted unknown-space gain, directional prior, object heat, a bonus for complementary views of UNCERTAIN candidates, minus A* action cost and teammate-history reuse; the top-K are kept.

Joint team assignment: over shortlist tuples, maximize a team objective (non-overlapping unknown gain, relevance, geodesic separation, minus action cost, history reuse and corridor conflict). Robots may take different task labels, and an ordered-assignment hysteresis margin (Δ=2) limits goal switching.

Candidate hypotheses: nodes are retained if they pass a raw score threshold and a robust z-score threshold (30% quantile baseline, MAD scale). Each candidate target instance becomes a persistent hypothesis with its evidence nodes, with bounded retries and cooldowns.

Structured single-node verification: an LLM (qwen3.7-plus) receives an oriented local occupancy ROI, projected instances with IDs and categories, and vertical cues. It returns YES/NO/UNCERTAIN plus bound support IDs, and a deterministic gate checks IDs, categories, predicate arity and per-clause verdicts.

Cross-node evidence aggregation: for an UNCERTAIN hypothesis, the union of the 4m x 4m node ROIs and the latest instance point caches are rendered as one evidence view and re-verified, so complementary clauses seen from different nodes or robots bind to one instance.
Final robot-target assignment: approach poses are sampled outside the verified instance, and Hungarian assignment on A* costs picks which robot goes to which target.

setting.backbone: qwen3-vl-embedding (semantic guidance) + qwen3.7-plus (structured relation verification), both frozen; Grounding DINO + MobileSAM in the real world
setting.observation: RGB-D 480x640 with poses, plus panoramas at topology nodes; shared occupancy map (0.075 m)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30°, with frontier goals planned by A*
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes); real robots for deployment
setting.privileged: In simulation, simulator-provided instance masks and IDs replace the detector and segmenter; real-world runs use learned perception.

results: CoRelNav reaches overall SR 0.513 and SPL 0.129 on mixed multi-task episodes, against VLN-Game (Dual) at 0.395 / 0.084, and uses about half the tokens (91.2k vs 189.5k per episode). For unconstrained exploration it beats Co-NavGPT, with the gap widest on cross-region episodes (SR 0.746 / SPL 0.252 vs 0.701 / 0.214).
limitations: Candidate-specific evidence acquisition starts only after a plausible target or support is observed, which can delay verification.
Aggregation cannot fully fix ambiguous geometry or viewpoint-dependent VLM relation errors.
Simulation uses oracle masks and IDs, and robustness to real detection, association and calibration errors is not quantified. Real-world evidence is a single qualitative demo on two robots.
